params.value: 31.22B total in the HF safetensors metadata (BF16 31,221,485,568 + F32 3,008). That includes the 1 MTP (nextn) layer. The main model alone is about 29.9B (Ollama model_type '29.9B', llama.cpp PR table 29.9B). The card calls it '30B-A3B', so about 3B active. From config, active per token is about 3.6B: about 1.8B non-expert excluding the input embedding, plus 4 of 64 routed experts x 46 MoE layers = 1.74B. Of the 29.9B in the main model, 27.8B are routed-expert parameters.

architecture.value: Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM (model_type glm4_moe_lite), a DeepSeek-V2-style MoE with MLA attention. Config: 47 layers, all full attention (no sliding-window or linear layers); first_k_dense_replace=1, so layer 0 is dense FFN (intermediate 10240) and 46 layers are MoE. Each MoE layer has 64 routed experts with top-4 routing (sigmoid/noaux_tc, routed_scaling 1.8) plus 1 shared expert, moe_intermediate 1536, hidden 2048. Attention: 20 heads, q_lora_rank 768, kv_lora_rank 512, qk_nope 192, qk_rope 64, v_head 256. num_nextn_predict_layers=1 (MTP), vocab 154880, rope_theta 1e6, no rope_scaling. KV cache (MLA latent) = (512+64) x 47 layers = 27,072 elements per token: 54,144 B/token at BF16, 27,072 B at FP8. llama.cpp converts it as arch DEEPSEEK2.

context_length.value: max_position_embeddings 202,752 (native, no rope_scaling, so there is no separate extended mode). The Z.ai docs say 200K context and 128K max output. Ollama lists 198K, Artificial Analysis 200,000.

modalities.value: Text in, text out only (pipeline_tag text-generation; Z.ai docs: input and output modalities Text; Ollama: 'Text input'). There is no vision tower, so all weights are language-model weights.

thinking.how_to_toggle: Thinking is on by default: the template's generation prompt ends '<|assistant|><think>' unless enable_thinking is defined and false, in which case it emits '</think>'. The template also has clear_thinking. By default it keeps reasoning only for assistant turns after the last user message (interleaved thinking within the current agent turn). clear_thinking=false keeps it for all turns, which is Z.ai 'Preserved Thinking'; the card asks for it on multi-turn agentic tasks. vLLM v0.33.0: per request, extra_body {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}. The glm47 parser engine (vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py lines 245-264) reads enable_thinking/thinking from chat kwargs and starts in CONTENT state. vLLM maps an incoming 'reasoning' or 'reasoning_content' history field back to reasoning_content for the template (vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py:361,619-658). llama.cpp b12418: per request "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}; server-wide --reasoning off or --reasoning-budget 0; --reasoning-preserve is on by default and its doc cites Z.ai preserved thinking. Ollama v0.40.16: native API "think": false; OpenAI endpoint "reasoning_effort": "none" maps to think=false for boolean models.

tool_calling.format: GLM XML: <tool_call>{name}<arg_key>k</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value>...</tool_call>. Tool results go back as <|observation|><tool_response>...</tool_response>.
tool_calling.evidence: The chat template renders the tools list: under 'if tools' it writes a '# Tools' system block that loops over tools with tojson inside <tools></tools>, and it renders assistant tool_calls and tool-role responses. The card serves with --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice and reports tau2-Bench 79.5. llama.cpp ships models/templates/GLM-4.7-Flash.jinja, byte-identical to the HF template (diff empty at b12418). Ollama shows the 'tools' badge with renderer/parser 'glm-4.7'. Ollama's own page offers 'ollama launch opencode --model glm-4.7-flash'.

vllm.arch_supported: Yes. registry.py at v0.33.0 line 125 has "Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM": ("glm4_moe_lite", ...) and line 730 has Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel for MTP. Added in commit 71832ba (PR #31386, 2026-01-19).
vllm.min_version: v0.15.0 (2026-01-29) is the first release tag that contains vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_moe_lite.py; v0.14.0 and v0.14.1 return 404. At launch the card said 'main branch only'.
vllm.tool_call_parser: glm47 (the card). In v0.33.0 vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py maps both glm45 and glm47 to Glm47MoeModelToolParser.
vllm.reasoning_parser: glm45 (the card) or glm47 (in-tree GLM-4.7 recipe). In v0.33.0 vllm/reasoning/__init__.py maps both to Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter, so the two names are equivalent.
vllm.best_checkpoint: Intel/GLM-4.7-Flash-int4-AutoRound (16.06 GiB), the smallest full-model vLLM checkpoint, used with expert CPU offload. Without offload nothing fits except the pruned REAP-23B NVFP4.
vllm.kv_math: Budget 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB. MLA KV = (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope 64) x 47 layers x 2 B = 54,144 B/token BF16, 27,072 B/token FP8. No checkpoint fits on the GPU alone. Intel int4 AutoRound: 14.65 - 16.06 - 1.2 = -2.61 GiB. QuantTrio AWQ 18.41 GiB: -4.96. axteam NVFP4A16 17.64 GiB: -4.19. Pruned REAP-23B NVFP4 (12.91 GiB): pool 0.54 GiB, which is 10,653 tokens BF16 or 21,307 FP8, too small for OpenCode. With UVA offload of experts (--cpu-offload-gb N --cpu-offload-params experts) on Intel int4: N=4 gives pool 1.39 GiB (27.5k BF16 / 55.0k FP8); N=6 gives pool 3.39 GiB (67.2k BF16 / 134.3k FP8); N=8 gives pool 5.39 GiB (106.8k BF16 / 202,752 FP8, capped by max_position_embeddings). An MTP spec layer, if enabled, adds 1 layer of KV plus its weights (about 1.3B params). Offloaded experts are read over PCIe 5.0 x16 (about 64 GB/s theoretical) through zero-copy UVA, so decode speed is speculative.
vllm.quant_on_sm120: Attention: on device_capability.major == 12, vLLM v0.33.0 cuda.py lines 134-137 selects TRITON_MLA (then FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120) for MLA, not FlashAttention 2. triton_mla.py accepts kv_cache_dtype fp8/fp8_e4m3 on SM89+ and dequantizes to BF16 on load. MoE weights: int4 AutoRound (GPTQ packing) and AWQ are expected to run through the Marlin W4A16 MoE kernels, which work on sm_120 (inferred, not traced in source). NVFP4 W4A4 builds would use the sm_120 FP4 paths with the FlashInfer JIT host-RAM caveat; NVFP4A16 uses Marlin FP4 (see open issue #34694 on NVFP4 Marlin garbled output on GPUs without native FP4, which does not apply to sm_120's native FP4).
vllm.serve_command: docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 -v $HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 Intel/GLM-4.7-Flash-int4-AutoRound --served-model-name glm-4.7-flash --max-model-len 65536 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --cpu-offload-gb 6 --cpu-offload-params experts --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45   (offload flags and KV numbers are from the arithmetic and have not been tested; the card's reference command is: vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 1 --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice --served-model-name glm-4.7-flash)
vllm.known_issues: Open vLLM issues on the glm47 parser family: #67684 (2026-11-14) drops tool calls with unknown function names and returns empty responses, trapping clients in retry loops; #67471 (2026-11-13) turns a quoted tag in prose into a real tool call with empty arguments; #60703 streaming parser swallows the rest of the stream after a stray <tool_call> token in prose; #49248 returns empty arguments when <arg_value> is omitted; #57826/#57827 drop the last parameter when the closing tag is missing; #63581 streamed tool_call index skips rejected calls (OpenAI SDK IndexError); #58315 required tool_choice grammar accepts split marker tokens; #65944 ModelOpt FP8 KV scales not loaded into MLA attention for GLM-4.7-Flash since v0.25.0. Not found: any open sm_120 issue specific to dense MLA with GLM-4.7-Flash; the sm_120 MLA issues concern sparse MLA in GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1.

llamacpp.arch_supported: Yes. Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM is converted as MODEL_ARCH.DEEPSEEK2 (conversion/glm.py line 248 at b12418, including MTP export). Support merged in PR #18936 (2026-01-19). Sigmoid gating fix #18980 (2026-01-21) is a loader fallback, so older GGUFs also load correctly. V-less MLA cache landed in #19067 (2026-01-25): llama-kv-cache.cpp has has_v = !is_mla, so only the 576-wide K latent is cached. CUDA FA for GLM 4.7 landed in #18953. Latest builds b12418/b12419 (2026-11-15) are marked prerelease on GitHub.
llamacpp.gguf_repo: unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF (Q4_K_M, 17.05 GiB), or UD-Q4_K_XL 16.32 GiB from the same repo
llamacpp.quant: Q4_K_M with --n-cpu-moe 17-18 at 64k context. Alternative fully on the GPU: UD-Q3_K_XL (12.84 GiB), which leaves about 1.97 GiB for KV, about 39k tokens at f16, too short for comfortable OpenCode use.
llamacpp.offload_plan: GPU available about 15.81 GiB (16303 - 112 MiB idle). Q4_K_M expert share: 17.05 x 27.78/29.92 / 46 = about 0.344 GiB per MoE layer. KV per token is 54,144 B at f16; q8_0 is about 28.8 KB. For 64k context with f16 KV (3.30 GiB) and a 1.0 GiB compute buffer, 5.54 GiB must move to RAM, so --n-cpu-moe 17 (5.85 GiB RAM). With q8_0 KV (1.76 GiB): --n-cpu-moe 12. For 128k: f16 KV 6.61 GiB needs --n-cpu-moe 26 (8.95 GiB RAM); q8_0 KV needs 17. For the full 202,752: f16 KV 10.22 GiB needs --n-cpu-moe 37 (12.7 GiB RAM); q8_0 needs 23. Everything stays well under the 40 GiB RAM budget. Using 18 instead of 17 adds headroom.
llamacpp.server_command: docker run --rm --gpus all -p 8080:8080 -v $HOME/models:/models ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13 -m /models/GLM-4.7-Flash-Q4_K_M.gguf --alias glm-4.7-flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 -ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe 18 -c 65536 -fa on --jinja --temp 0.7 --top-p 1.0 --min-p 0.01   (unsloth's tool-calling sampling is temp 0.7 / top-p 1.0; the card uses the same for SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench; add -ctk q8_0 to halve KV and drop --n-cpu-moe to about 12, after testing that quantized K works with MLA)
llamacpp.tool_calling_note: Works through --jinja (on by default) with the embedded template. llama.cpp ships models/templates/GLM-4.7-Flash.jinja, byte-identical to the HF template, and its test-chat suite covers it (open issue #30313 is a test-harness skip, not a runtime bug). Open #20650 reports '500 - Failed to parse input' on some tool calls; the GLM-4.7-Flash link there is not confirmed. Reasoning is returned in reasoning_content; --reasoning-preserve (default on) supports Z.ai preserved thinking.

speed_notes: Measured, RTX 4090 (not 50-series), llama.cpp PR #30489: GLM-4.7-Flash Q4_K prefill pp2048 about 8,440-8,590 t/s fully on the GPU (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30489). Measured, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GB), PR #30196: unsloth GLM-4.7-Flash Q8_0 with MTP speculative decoding gave about 128-130 t/s mean decode on SPEED-Bench coding turns (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30196). PR #31968's 43 t/s figures are from SYCL (Intel GPU) and do not apply. Bandwidth arithmetic (inferred): active about 3.56B params per token; at Q4_K_M (~4.9 bpw) that is about 2.18 GB read per token. Fully on the GPU: 896 GB/s / 2.18 GB = about 410 t/s ceiling. With --n-cpu-moe 18: about 0.42 GB per token comes from DDR5 (18 layers x 4 experts x 5.78 MB). At 80 GB/s that is 5.2 ms, plus about 2.0 ms of GPU time, so the ceiling is about 140 t/s and realistic decode is perhaps 40-80 t/s. With --n-cpu-moe 28 the ceiling is about 100 t/s. MLA decode slows with depth (the SYCL table shows 43 to 25-32 t/s from 0 to 16k depth), so expect lower rates at OpenCode-scale contexts. vLLM with UVA expert offload reads experts over PCIe 5.0 and is unmeasured.

opencode_fit.caveats: 1) Q4 weights (16-17 GiB) exceed 16 GB VRAM, so experts must be partly in system RAM: no all-GPU build at Q4. In vLLM nothing full-size fits without offload. 2) Thinking is on by default. OpenCode must send the reasoning back for interleaved thinking within a turn. vLLM maps 'reasoning' to reasoning_content and llama.cpp preserves it by default; whether OpenCode v2.3.0 sends it is unverified. 3) The vLLM glm47 tool parser has several open bugs (#67684 empty response on unknown tool names, #60703 stream swallowed after a stray <tool_call>, #67471 prose tag becomes a call); prefer llama.cpp or Ollama. 4) Vendor numbers (SWE-bench Verified 59.2, tau2 79.5) are self-reported. Independent AA results are modest (Terminal-Bench Hard 22%; GPQA 58 vs vendor 75), and AA marks the model deprecated in favour of GLM-5. 5) Released 2026-01-19, about 10 months old; newer 30B-A3B class models may beat it. 6) Use temp 0.7 / top-p 1.0 for agentic coding (the card's SWE-bench setting).

Whether llama.cpp accepts -ctk q8_0 for the V-less MLA cache on CUDA, and its quality impact, was not verified.
No measured decode speed on an RTX 5080 Laptop GPU or with --n-cpu-moe offload; the speeds are bandwidth estimates.
No independent SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.x, BFCL or Aider results were found for GLM-4.7-Flash; the AA Intelligence Index is null (model marked deprecated).
Whether Ollama v0.40.16 offloads only expert tensors (rather than whole layers) for this model on a 16 GB GPU was not checked.
OpenCode v2.3.0 behavior with the GLM reasoning round-trip and tool_choice (issue #60202) was not tested for this model.
